components.note: Kasm's own Postgres: users, settings, workspaces and sessions.
The web API and the manager that schedules sessions.
Starts the workspace containers on this machine.

RDP, VNC and SSH to other machines. No workspace here uses it. Kasm's all-in-one install starts it, so it is carried; dropping it means installing the roles separately (db, app, agent, proxy), which is not built.

plugins.note: The network sidecar (VPN and egress features). Nothing offered here uses it; the installer installs it regardless.

registry.name: Baseline
registry.description: Workspaces carried by this Baseline host, and a reviewed few from LinuxServer.io.

_note: Copy to config/local/kasm-recipe.json (git-ignored) and edit; the build then uses it. states: required (Kasm does not run without it), used, unused (carried because the all-in-one install starts it). settings: server settings to set at install (not secrets). registry: when enabled, Kasm is pointed at Baseline's own workspace registry (list_url empty means this host's own address). registry.sources: other registries whose NAMED workspaces are offered through it (kasm_sources.py): each workspace is pinned to the hash of the definition that was read (run the build once, read the report, copy the hash into reviewed) and each run-configuration property it adds must be accepted by name. These images are not carried: they are pulled from their own registry when first started (internet needed). A Kasm entry in the supported-OS list may name the workspaces instead.
